voice-rain-location.text: Rain softened the city beyond MJ’s window. Inside, there was nowhere for either of them to hide.

voice-distance.text: She kept the couch between them. Spider-Man stayed by the door, injured and careful not to come closer.

voice-room-reading-choice.text: Before either of them spoke, the room had already chosen what it would reveal.

voice-threshold-reading.text: The door stayed within reach. If she wanted the conversation over, he would be the one who moved.

voice-mj-grip-reading.text: Her fingers stayed at the seam of her jacket: one small boundary that still belonged entirely to her.

voice-mj-boundary.text: You remember a life with me. I remember a stranger making choices for me.

voice-peter-mask-thought.text: The mask made danger simple. Peter Parker was the part that could still ask to be forgiven.

voice-peter-protection.text: I came to warn you, not to make you believe me. What happened to your memory was my decision—and it was wrong.

voice-unmask.text: He removed the mask. The hero did not leave; he became visibly human.

voice-name.text: My name is Peter Parker. I loved you before the spell. That truth belongs to me; it does not obligate you.

voice-name-reading-choice.text: The name entered the room once. It landed in two different histories.

voice-peter-name-private.text: For four years, Peter Parker had been the name he removed from every life he touched. Saying it without demanding recognition felt like returning evidence, not reclaiming a place.

voice-mj-name-private.text: The name explained the grief in his face. It did not place a memory in hers—and he had finally left that difference intact.

voice-name-settles.text: MJ repeated the name once, quietly. Peter did not move closer.

voice-name-settles-v1.text: MJ repeated the name once, testing its weight. Peter heard it return without mistaking sound for recognition.

voice-name-settles-v2.text: MJ repeated the stranger’s name carefully. It identified the person before her without manufacturing a shared past.

voice-mj-sees.text: His face carried the grief of recognition. Mine could only answer with sympathy.

voice-mj-answer.text: I can understand why the girl in your memories loved you. But I am standing here without them.

voice-perspective-choice.text: The same silence held two different losses.

voice-peter-restraint.text: Love could explain why he stayed. It could not grant permission to decide for her again.

voice-mj-boundary-private.text: Being grateful for his sacrifice did not require inheriting another woman’s answer.

voice-both-truths-reading.text: He could love her and still have wronged her. She could honour the sacrifice and still refuse the life it presumed. Understanding made neither truth disappear.

voice-both-truths-reading-v1.text: Peter’s restraint had made love look costly. MJ’s boundary then revealed why cost could not purchase consent. Holding both truths made neither disappear.

voice-both-truths-reading-v2.text: MJ’s boundary had made memory’s absence decisive. Peter’s restraint then revealed love learning not to overrule it. Holding both truths made neither disappear.

voice-room-without-verdict.text: Neither of them named the pause forgiveness. For the first time, the room did not require one pain to overrule the other.

voice-shared-silence.text: A distant siren crossed the rain. Peter lowered the mask. MJ did not step back—but she did not close the distance.

voice-shared-silence-v1.text: A distant siren crossed the rain. Peter lowered the mask and kept the distance he had finally learned not to cross.

voice-shared-silence-v2.text: A distant siren crossed the rain. MJ did not step back—but kindness did not become consent to a remembered life.

voice-shared-silence-v3.text: A distant siren crossed the rain. Peter lowered the mask. MJ stayed. The distance between them remained real and, for once, mutually visible.

voice-small-defence-returns.text: The couch still divided the room. Neither of them treated the pause as permission.

voice-small-defence-returns-v1.text: The path to the door remained open behind Peter. What first looked like distance now read as a promise that MJ would never have to move around him.

voice-small-defence-returns-v2.text: MJ’s hand loosened at her jacket seam. The movement was not forgiveness; it was one defence becoming unnecessary.

voice-small-defence-returns-v3.text: The exit remained open behind Peter as MJ’s hand loosened at her jacket seam. Two small defences changed without either becoming surrender.

voice-restraint-forecast.text: The silence had become legible enough to risk a prediction.

voice-forecast-retreat.text: You read the open door as preparation to vanish before her answer could hurt him.

voice-forecast-return-choice.text: You read the open door as evidence that staying no longer required him to control the exit.

voice-peter-offers-distance.text: I can call a cab. Or I can take you home. You choose.

voice-peter-offers-distance-v1.text: Peter looked toward the open door, then stayed. “I can call a cab. Or I can take you home. You choose.”

voice-peter-offers-distance-v2.text: Peter left the open door behind him and the decision with her. “I can call a cab. Or I can take you home. You choose.”

voice-ride-home.text: I still need to get home. Can you take me?

voice-departure-decision.text: Help could still become control in the distance between an offer and a door. The departure needed one rule Peter could not reinterpret for her.

voice-ordinary-route-reading.text: No web, no window, no spectacular rescue. If he meant to return the choice, he could survive the slow indignity of the stairs.

voice-visible-route-reading.text: Leaving first would spare him the answer and make her carry his absence again. This time, he would remain until she dismissed him.

voice-mj-names-route.text: The stairs. No webbing. Stay where I can see you.

voice-door-opens.text: MJ opened the apartment door herself. The hallway was dry, ordinary, and bright enough to make every step accountable.

voice-hallway-threshold.text: She crossed first. Peter followed one full pace behind, the mask loose at his side.

voice-hallway-threshold-v1.text: She crossed first and chose the stairs. Peter followed one full pace behind, accepting an ordinary route he could not optimize into a rescue.

voice-hallway-threshold-v2.text: She crossed first. Peter stayed one full pace behind and plainly visible, refusing the old instinct to make pain disappear by disappearing himself.

voice-mj-corrects-promise.text: Taking me home is not a promise about tomorrow. It is one walk, tonight.

voice-peter-hears-limit.text: Once, he would have heard the limit as a door closing. Now he heard its other meaning: she had trusted him with something small enough not to own.

voice-peter-accepts-limit.text: One walk. Tonight. You set the pace.

voice-stairs-begin.text: MJ turned toward the stairwell. Peter waited for her first step, then matched neither her stride nor her silence—only the distance she had chosen.

voice-ending.text: He could protect her without possessing her answer. The city below still needed Spider-Man; the next stair required only Peter Parker to stay one pace behind.

voice-plea-reading.text: You heard the name reach for her: a claim, quietly made, waiting for its echo.

voice-name-settles-v3.text: MJ repeated the name once, quietly. Peter did not move closer, and did not wait for it to come back changed.

voice-mj-answer-v1.text: I can understand why the girl in your memories loved you. You are not asking me to be her—I can hear that. But I am standing here without them.

voice-mj-debt-reading.text: You read her stillness as a debt being counted: a man had erased himself for her, and gratitude was waiting for its shape.

voice-shared-silence-v4.text: A distant siren crossed the rain. Peter lowered the mask. MJ did not step back—and nothing in her stillness was counting.

voice-forecast-plead.text: You read the lowered mask as the last step before asking: try. Just try to remember.

voice-peter-offers-distance-v3.text: Peter did not ask her to remember. “I can call a cab. Or I can take you home. You choose.”

voice-swing-route-reading.text: You wanted him to carry her home above the streets, the one gift only he could give. MJ’s rule went the other way.

voice-door-opens-v1.text: MJ opened the apartment door herself. The hallway was dry, ordinary, and bright enough to make every step accountable—no window, no sky, nothing that only he could do.

voice-hallway-threshold-v3.text: She crossed first and took the stairs. Peter followed one full pace behind, the rooftops he could have offered her left unmentioned.

voice-mj-corrects-promise-v1.text: Taking me home is not a promise about tomorrow, and it is not a payment. It is one walk, tonight.

voice-stairs-begin-v1.text: MJ turned toward the stairwell. Peter had asked her for nothing—not even to remember. He waited for her first step, then matched neither her stride nor her silence—only the distance she had chosen.
